# TDPdf v1.29.0.0

**Windows are now identifiable, tabs are now readable at a glance, and documents can move between windows with a drag.**

## The open document was invisible outside the app

With one PDF open, nothing on screen told you which file it was unless you looked closely at the small label next to the logo. Worse, the actual window title — the text Alt-Tab and the taskbar show — never changed from "TDPdf" no matter what was open. Two windows, each holding a different set of documents, looked identical everywhere except inside the app itself.

The window title now reflects the active document, plus how many other tabs share that window. Alt-Tab and the taskbar can tell your windows apart now.

## Tabs are easier to work with

- Hovering a tab shows its full filename, so a long name cut short by the tab strip doesn't have to be guessed at.
- A new dropdown on the tab strip lists every open tab by name — useful once there are more tabs open than fit on screen at once.

## Move a document to another window with a drag

TDPdf already supported multiple independent windows (each launch is its own window and its own process, unless "Single Instance Tabs" folds a second launch into the first). What was missing was any way to *move* a document from one window to another without closing and reopening it.

Drag a tab onto another open TDPdf window, and the document moves there. Drop it anywhere else — or use "Move to New Window" from the tab's right-click menu — and it tears off into a brand-new window. This is what makes grouping documents into separate windows practical: five files in one window, eight in another, three in a third, rearranged by dragging rather than by hand.

A document with unsaved changes is saved to its real file first (you'll be asked, the same way closing a tab with unsaved changes already asks); a document that has never been saved is asked to be saved first rather than moved silently, since there is nowhere on disk yet to hand over.

## Already there, in case it wasn't obvious

Opening several files at once was already fully supported before this release: File → Open's dialog accepts a multi-selection, and dragging multiple files (or a folder, or a zip) onto TDPdf opens all of them. No change was needed there — if this wasn't discoverable, now you know.
